name: SmugMug
tagline: Publish a self-hosted client gallery from user-owned photo storage

tiers.name: Direct
tiers.limits: Unlimited full-resolution JPEG storage; digital delivery; Lightroom integration and 24/7 support.
tiers.notes: Annual total is $240; the live page exposes a monthly toggle but did not render its monthly price.

tiers.name: Portfolio
tiers.limits: Unlimited JPEG storage plus print/digital sales, a customizable site, watermarks and fulfillment.
tiers.notes: Annual total is $282; the live page exposes a monthly toggle but did not render its monthly price.

tiers.name: Pro
tiers.limits: Unlimited JPEG storage plus multiple pricelists, coupons/packages and client favoriting/download controls.
tiers.notes: Annual total is $444; the live page exposes a monthly toggle but did not render its monthly price.

tiers.name: Enterprise
tiers.limits: Custom volume, team and institutional terms; 0 self-serve prices published.

pricing.billingTerms: monthly + annual; only annual-equivalent prices rendered in the live public page
pricing.hiddenCosts: RAW storage is an add-on: $10/month for the first 1 TB, then $6/month for each additional TB.

verdictSummary: A consolation build is possible, but the paid product's decisive value sits outside a solo rebuild. For SmugMug, publish a self-hosted client gallery from user-owned photo storage. The hard boundary is image hosting, global delivery, print commerce, client proofing, and support, plus image pipeline quality, models, and workflow polish.
coreLoopDIY: Catalog local photos from user-owned storage, generate previews, apply non-destructive adjustments, and publish selected images to a self-hosted client gallery.
whatYouLose: image hosting, global delivery, print commerce, client proofing, and support
moatNotes: image pipeline quality, models, and workflow polish
ongoingBurden: raw codecs, color management, metadata, previews, face models, GPU support, storage, backups, sync, and export fidelity
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for SmugMug because photographers pay because image quality, catalog safety, and fast handling of huge libraries matter more than cloning sliders. The recurring cost buys raw codecs, color management, metadata, previews, face models, GPU support, storage, backups, sync, and export fidelity, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: Immich
priorArt.desc: Active open-source self-hosted photo and video management platform.

alternatives.name: Lychee
alternatives.desc: Clean albums, passworded shares, metadata, and downloads from your own storage; no print lab, sales engine, or hand-holding.

facts.install: Docker Compose with the Lychee image and MariaDB; prebuilt and source installs also exist
facts.dataFormat: Uploaded originals and derivatives live in persistent uploads storage; albums, users, metadata and settings live in MariaDB (or another configured database), with separate logs and temporary-data volumes
facts.gapVsPaid: It can publish attractive private albums, but it has no SmugMug print lab, storefront, client proofing, sales fulfillment or managed hosting support.
facts.setupBlocker: Docker Compose, writable persistent volumes, a database, an APP_KEY, and domain/TLS setup for remote sharing

alternatives.name: Photoview
alternatives.desc: A fast gallery over an existing folder tree with RAW, EXIF, users, share links, and downloads; minimal branding controls, maximum ownership.

facts.install: Docker Compose with SQLite, MariaDB, or PostgreSQL and one or more mounted media folders
facts.engines: Built-in dlib/go-face face detection and recognition; FFmpeg for video processing; optional Mapbox token for maps
facts.dataFormat: Original photos remain in the mounted folder tree; the database stores users, albums, indexes, and face metadata, while a media-cache directory stores thumbnails and optimized video
facts.gapVsPaid: It is an ownership-first browser over your folders, not SmugMug's branded portfolio, print-sales, proofing and fulfillment business platform.
facts.setupBlocker: Docker plus careful volume paths and host-file permissions; safe remote access also needs a reverse proxy or VPN and TLS

alternatives.name: Piwigo
alternatives.desc: A mature self-hosted gallery with private albums, users, themes, metadata, downloads, and a huge plugin ecosystem; you become the support desk.

facts.install: Upload the NetInstall script or release to PHP web hosting, then complete browser setup against MySQL or MariaDB
facts.dataFormat: Originals live under the upload or galleries directories, generated derivatives and configuration stay in the Piwigo tree, and albums, users, metadata, and plugin state live in MySQL or MariaDB
facts.gapVsPaid: Themes and plugins can approximate galleries, but SmugMug's integrated commerce, print lab, proofing and fully managed hosting do not come with it.
facts.setupBlocker: Requires PHP web hosting, a database, writable directories, and ongoing web-server, TLS, and plugin maintenance

rejectedAlternatives.name: Immich
rejectedAlternatives.desc: Excellent backup and browsing, but client-facing gallery theming, password workflows, and presentation polish are afterthoughts.

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Power plan and a personal local photo catalog DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a closest honest personal substitute for SmugMug in an empty repository.
Use Tauri 2, React, TypeScript, Rust image libraries, SQLite, and local filesystem access; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: catalog local photos from user-owned storage, generate previews, apply non-destructive adjustments, and publish selected images to a self-hosted client gallery.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Index selected folders without moving or rewriting originals and store only catalog data in SQLite.
Generate thumbnails and previews, read EXIF, detect duplicates by hash, and monitor file changes.
Provide timeline, folders, albums, ratings, flags, tags, search, and side-by-side compare.
Store edits as reversible parameters for crop, rotate, exposure, contrast, white balance, and saturation.
Render exports to a new folder with explicit color space, quality, size, and metadata choices.
Add catalog backup, missing-file repair, integrity scan, and a clear original-safety guarantee.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Do not claim to reproduce proprietary data, network liquidity, regulated access, or frontier infrastructure.
Deliberately leave out a proprietary raw-rendering engine.
Deliberately leave out hosted cross-device photo sync and client galleries.
Deliberately leave out frontier culling, retouching, and generative models.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
